name: Vanta Ordnance Void Screamer VS-3 'Banshee Wire'
description:
A hybrid sonic-kinetic weapon that fires a monofilament wire at hypersonic speed, creating a devastating sonic shockwave along the wire's flight path. The Void Screamer launches a 50-meter spool of carbon-nanotube monofilament that unspools at Mach 2, generating a focused sonic boom in a narrow corridor along its trajectory.

Vanta Ordnance designed the VS-3 to combine the cutting capability of monofilament with the area-of-effect characteristics of sonic weapons. The wire itself is nearly invisible and sharp enough to cut through light armor, while the shockwave it generates stuns and disorients targets within 5 meters of the flight path. The result is a weapon that cuts and concusses simultaneously.

The Banshee Wire's firing mechanism is a compressed-gas launcher that deploys the monofilament spool through a magnetic guide that controls the wire's trajectory. The wire is single-use — after deployment, it falls to the ground as a nearly invisible hazard until collected. Post-engagement cleanup is as important as the firing itself, as loose monofilament can cause accidental amputations.
base_technologies: Sonic shockwave generation from wire velocity
specifications:
caliber: N/A — 50-meter carbon-nanotube monofilament spool
effective_range: 10-50 meters (wire length)
rate_of_fire: 1 spool per 4 seconds (reload required)
capacity: 6 spools
weight: 5.8 kg
power_source: Compressed-gas launcher, 6 deployments per cartridge
tactical_use: The Banshee Wire is deployed in ambush scenarios and corridor denial where its dual cutting/stunning effect maximizes disruption. The monofilament cuts through the first target it contacts, while the sonic shockwave incapacitates nearby personnel. In enclosed spaces, the shockwave reflects off walls and amplifies, extending the weapon's area of effect. Operators must exercise extreme caution with post-deployment wire location — several friendly-fire incidents have involved personnel walking into deployed monofilament.
cultural_context: The Void Screamer represents Vanta Ordnance's continued innovation at the intersection of conventional and exotic weapons technology. The weapon's dramatic deployment — a screaming wire that cuts and stuns — has earned it a reputation that exceeds its tactical utility. The phrase 'getting wired' has entered GLMZ slang to describe being caught in an inescapable trap, and the distinctive shriek of a hypersonic monofilament deployment is one of the most recognizable sounds in urban combat.
story_hooks: A deployed Banshee Wire was left uncollected in a pedestrian corridor. By the time it was discovered, nine people had walked through it, suffering injuries ranging from deep lacerations to partial amputations. The operator who deployed it claims the engagement was sanctioned — the cleanup crew claims they were never dispatched.

Someone has developed a guided monofilament spool that uses micro-thrusters to steer the wire around corners and through doorways. The modified VS-3 can deploy its wire through non-linear paths, making the weapon effective around corners and through obstacles.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, angular launcher resembling a hybrid between a rifle and a specialized deployment system. The profile is aggressive and forward-swept, with a pronounced muzzle housing that appears to breathe or pulse. The weapon has an almost organic quality — sharp edges meet smooth curves in a design that suggests controlled violence.
physical_description.dimensions: 127 cm overall length, 8 cm width at the widest point (breach), 6.5 cm height at charging handle. Muzzle assembly extends 18 cm from the receiver. Spool cartridge sits elevated above the bore axis.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but balanced — 5.8 kg distributed across the frame creates a weapon that feels grounded and purposeful in the shoulder. The compressed-gas system adds weight forward, creating a natural pivot point around the grip.
physical_description.primary_material: Titanium-reinforced polymer composite chassis with steel breech assembly and magnetic guide rails. Carbon-nanotube spool housing visible through transparent polymer viewport.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal with brushed steel breech and guide rails. Thermal-reactive paint on the muzzle assembly shifts from deep charcoal to dark blue under stress, indicating pressure buildup.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte charcoal-black primary with silver-steel accents on the breech block, gas coupling, and rail system. The spool housing window reveals the wound monofilament as a faint crystalline shimmer.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer grip with integrated pressure sensors — rough, aggressive texturing that grips even sweaty or augmented hands. Rubberized charging handle with defined serrations.
distinctive_features: Transparent polycarbonate viewport revealing the wound monofilament spool — shows the nearly-invisible wire in faint reflections
Forward-mounted magnetic guide cage — a series of small electromagnetic coils visible along the top of the barrel housing
Pressure readout display integrated into the left side of the receiver — small red-to-green gradient bar indicating gas cartridge depletion
Sonic resonance chamber at the muzzle — honeycomb porting designed to amplify shockwave generation
Spool cartridge ejection port with spring-loaded mechanism on the right side
Heat-sink fins along the muzzle assembly in a triangular pattern, giving it a predatory aesthetic
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: VANTA ORDNANCE logo etched into the left side of the receiver in italicized chrome lettering. Serial number plate stamped into the titanium breech block. Small monofilament hazard symbol (three parallel lines with a warning triangle) embossed near the muzzle.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-ready and pristine when deployed, though many operator examples show faint scoring along the guide rails from repeated monofilament deployment. The spool housing may show micro-scratches from high-velocity wire unspooling. Gas coupling shows minor corrosion from humidity in the GLMZ climate — a bronze patina develops with age.
